Composition and differential abundance

Songqi Duan

duan@songqi.org Source: vignettes/composition-analysis.Rmd
composition-analysis.Rmd

Composition analysis should not treat every cell as an independent biological replicate. Shennong separates cell-level counting from sample-level comparison: first compute proportions, then compare replicate samples.

This article uses the public Kotliarov PBMC CITE-seq subset. The 20 real_sample values are biological replicates, and each sample has one source-study real_response value. Cell counts are never treated as replicate counts for the response comparison.

Prepare cluster labels and sample metadata 

library(Shennong)
library(Seurat)
library(dplyr)

pbmc <- qs2::qs_read(real_data_file)

pbmc <- sn_run_cluster(
  object = pbmc,
  normalization_method = "seurat",
  nfeatures = 1500,
  dims = 1:15,
  resolution = 0.6,
  species = "human",
  verbose = FALSE
)
sample_design <- pbmc[[]] |>
  dplyr::distinct(real_sample, real_response) |>
  dplyr::arrange(real_sample)

sample_design

The design table above is the source-study metadata used below. Its one-row-per- sample structure makes the inferential unit explicit.

Count cells before comparing groups

sn_calculate_composition() returns a transparent table with group totals, category counts, and percentages.

composition <- sn_calculate_composition(
  x = pbmc,
  group_by = "real_sample",
  variable = "seurat_clusters",
  min_cells = 10,
  measure = "both"
)

head(composition)

The denominator is visible in group_total, which makes it easy to audit whether a proportion is based on enough cells.

Observed-over-expected enrichment is useful when you want to ask which clusters are enriched or depleted relative to the full contingency table.

roe <- sn_calculate_roe(
  x = pbmc,
  group_by = "real_response",
  variable = "seurat_clusters"
)

head(roe)
roe_matrix <- sn_calculate_roe(
  x = pbmc,
  group_by = "real_response",
  variable = "seurat_clusters",
  return_matrix = TRUE
)

roe_matrix[, seq_len(min(4, ncol(roe_matrix))), drop = FALSE]
sn_plot_composition(
  pbmc,
  x = real_sample,
  fill = seurat_clusters,
  position = "stack",
  palette = "Paired",
  title = "PBMC cluster composition by real biological sample"
)

The plotting helper can also keep the biological sample as the replicate. The following computes per-sample cluster proportions from metadata, fills absent sample/cluster combinations with zero, and then draws the sample distributions within each response group.

sn_plot_composition(
  pbmc,
  x = real_response,
  fill = seurat_clusters,
  type = "sample_boxplot",
  sample_by = "real_sample",
  show_points = TRUE
)

Use type = "sample_bar" with errorbar = "se" or "sd" when a mean-with-error display is required. Use type = "alluvial" and flow_by = c("level1", "level2", "level3") to audit hierarchical annotation or source-to-final-label flows; no optional Sankey backend is needed.

Compare sample-level proportions

sn_compare_composition() summarizes each sample first, then compares those sample-level proportions between conditions. That avoids pseudo-replication.

comparison <- sn_compare_composition(
  x = pbmc,
  sample_by = "real_sample",
  group_by = "real_response",
  variable = "seurat_clusters",
  contrast = c("d0 high", "d0 low"),
  min_cells = 20,
  test = "wilcox"
)

comparison

Use the plotting helpers for the summary table when you want a compact figure-ready view.

sn_plot_barplot(
  comparison,
  x = seurat_clusters,
  y = log2_fc,
  fill = change,
  stat = "identity",
  palette = "Set2",
  angle_x = 45,
  y_label = "log2 fold-change",
  title = "Composition shift: high vs low responders"
)

Compare continuous metadata with boxplots

Composition is categorical. For continuous per-cell or per-sample summaries, summarize to the replicate level first, then plot.

sample_qc <- pbmc[[]] |>
  dplyr::group_by(real_sample, real_response) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_features = median(nFeature_RNA),
    median_mito = median(pctMT),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

sn_plot_boxplot(
  sample_qc,
  x = real_response,
  y = median_features,
  y_label = "Median detected genes",
  title = "Per-sample QC summary by response group"
)

Local differential abundance with miloR

Global proportions can miss local shifts inside an embedding. sn_run_milo() wraps the miloR neighborhood workflow for sample-level differential abundance. Because miloR is optional, these chunks run only in the all profile when the backend is installed.

milo_result <- sn_run_milo(
  x = pbmc,
  sample_by = "real_sample",
  group_by = "real_response",
  contrast = c("d0 high", "d0 low"),
  reduction = "pca",
  dims = 1:15,
  annotation_by = "seurat_clusters",
  max_cells = 1500,
  seed = 717,
  return_object = FALSE
)

head(sn_get_milo_result(milo_result))

return_object = FALSE returns a complete result; use sn_get_milo_result() for its table. Add keep_model = TRUE to retain the fitted Milo object in milo_result$models$milo. The seed controls sampling and neighborhood selection.

The real neighborhood result can be stored and retrieved with the same object-level convention used for DE and enrichment.

pbmc <- sn_store_result(
  object = pbmc, type = "milo",
  result = milo_result, result_id = "response_da"
)
sn_list_results(pbmc, type = "milo")

head(sn_get_milo_result(pbmc, result_id = "response_da"))

sn_plot_milo() then displays the stored neighborhood-level table.

sn_plot_milo(
  pbmc,
  result_id = "response_da",
  annotation_by = "seurat_clusters",
  title = "Neighborhood differential abundance"
)

The recommended reporting pattern is to show both global composition and local neighborhood abundance when a biological claim depends on changes in cell-state frequency.

Dedicated composition functions and Sankey presets

Use column-name strings throughout the composition family. Strings held in variables work too; no aes() or unquoted column expressions are needed.

Unified type Dedicated entry point
"sankey" / "alluvial" sn_plot_sankey()
"bar" / "stacked_bar" sn_plot_bar()
"sample_bar" / "errorbar" sn_plot_sample_bar()
"sample_boxplot" sn_plot_sample_boxplot()
"histogram" sn_plot_histogram()

These entry points share the same counting, replicate-aware summaries and figure metadata as sn_plot_composition(). The existing sn_plot_barplot() and sn_plot_boxplot() remain generic numeric-data plotters.

sn_plot_bar(pbmc, x_by = "real_sample", fill_by = "seurat_clusters")
sn_plot_sample_bar(pbmc, x_by = "real_response", fill_by = "seurat_clusters",
                   sample_by = "real_sample", errorbar = "se")
sn_plot_sample_boxplot(pbmc, x_by = "real_response", fill_by = "seurat_clusters",
                       sample_by = "real_sample")
sn_plot_histogram(pbmc, x_by = "nCount_RNA", bins = 30)

The unified equivalent accepts the same selectors, e.g. sn_plot_composition(pbmc, x_by = "real_sample", fill_by = "seurat_clusters"). Legacy x, y, fill, and facet mappings remain compatible there, but cannot be combined with their *_by replacements. Dedicated functions accept only string selectors. For summarized weights use y_by = "count" (or your numeric column name) on a data frame; Seurat inputs count individual cells.

style Layout Default flow colors
"A" Separated hierarchy; two or more stages First stage
"B" Left/right annotation comparison with brackets; two stages Final stage
"C" Top/bottom composition, colored bars and pies; two stages First stage

A retains the sankey_layout = "expanded" option: extra node whitespace makes axes with more categories taller without changing count widths. B uses tighter spacing and external brackets. Both accept axis_labels = c("Original", "Final"). All styles retain independent factor order: top-to-bottom in A/B, left-to-right in C. Character columns retain first appearance order.

sn_plot_sankey(pbmc, flow_by = c("real_response", "seurat_clusters"),
               style = "C", show_legend = FALSE)

For annotation comparisons and hierarchies, substitute your metadata columns:

sn_plot_sankey(seurat_obj,
  flow_by = c("cell_type_level1", "cell_type_level2"),
  fill_by = "cell_type_level1", style = "A", sankey_layout = "expanded")
sn_plot_sankey(seurat_obj,
  flow_by = c("original_label", "final_annotation"), style = "B",
  axis_labels = c("Original label", "Final annotation"))
sn_plot_sankey(seurat_obj,
  flow_by = c("age_group", "cell_type"), style = "C",
  palette = c(Young = "#7F8C8D", Aged = "#55A5D8"),
  facet_row_by = "compartment", show_legend = FALSE)

C pies have equal size and show each target category’s source-group proportions, computed from the same retained weights as the ribbons within each facet. Use show_pies = FALSE to omit them and node_palette to color target bars independently. C requires source-based fill_by so ribbon and pie colors agree. Each C facet is scaled to the same horizontal span; widths encode relative composition within a facet, not comparable absolute counts between facets. C uses aspect_ratio as the fixed coordinate ratio (default 0.45) so pies remain circular. show_stratum_boxes = TRUE outlines its colored node bars.

Missing paths are excluded; replace missing annotations with "Unknown" to retain them. Use a taller/wider export when many or long labels need more room.

Panel sizing

All five dedicated composition entry points and sn_plot_composition() accept panel_widths and panel_heights explicitly, in points (pt). These control the drawing panel, excluding outer labels and margins, and do not require catplot. For example:

sn_plot_sankey(seurat_obj,
  flow_by = c("cell_type_level1", "cell_type_level2"), style = "B",
  panel_widths = 320, panel_heights = 400, show_legend = FALSE)

Scalars apply to every facet. A/B and the other composition plots also accept vectors for facet column widths and row heights. Style C requires scalar sizes so all pies remain circular. Supplying both sizes takes precedence over aspect_ratio. With one size and an aspect ratio the other is derived; C also derives a missing size using its default coordinate ratio. Export to a canvas large enough to include the panel plus labels, title, legend and margins.

Eight-point text and optional pies

All composition plot text defaults to 8 pt, including axes, titles, legends, facet strips and Sankey node labels. C-style source headings use the same size. For backward compatibility stratum_label_size still takes millimeters; its new default is 8 / ggplot2::.pt to produce 8 pt text.

C-style bottom pies are optional through an explicit sn_plot_sankey() argument:

sn_plot_sankey(seurat_obj, flow_by = c("age_group", "cell_type"),
               style = "C", show_pies = FALSE)  # no pies
sn_plot_sankey(seurat_obj, flow_by = c("age_group", "cell_type"),
               style = "C", show_pies = TRUE)   # include pies (C default)

Toggling pies preserves the ribbons and their underlying cell counts.

Retrieve one Milo annotation

The column supplied to sn_store_milo(annotation_by = "cell_type") also controls annotation filtering during retrieval. Annotation and spatial FDR filters can be used independently. Missing stored annotation columns cause an explicit error when annotation filtering is requested.

sn_list_results(pbmc, type = "milo")
sn_get_milo_result(pbmc, "response_da", annotation = "Tcell")
